title: [Bounty $5k] ttnn.log_sigmoid: 0.91% peak fp32 error and a missing x <= -4 branch
body:
## Summary `ttnn.log_sigmoid` has three accuracy defects in its current SFPU kernel. A source-level model over two million fp32 inputs on `[-30, 30]` gives: | implementation | max relative error | max fp32 ULP vs PyTorch | |---|---:|---:| | current kernel | 9.13e-3 | 131,755 | | proposed fix, fused MAD model | 2.15e-7 | 2.0 | | proposed fix, non-fused MAD model | 2.34e-7 | 2.0 | ULP is `|actual - expected| / ULP(expected)`, the definition used by `assert_with_ulp`. The expected output is the registered golden, `torch.nn.functional.logsigmoid` ([`unary.py#L63`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/ttnn/ttnn/operations/unary.py#L63)). The binding advertises `FLOAT32` without a range caveat ([`unary_nanobind.cpp#L1863-L1868`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/eltwise/unary/unary_nanobind.cpp#L1863-L1868)). This is primarily an fp32 defect. Modelled bf16 error is 2.1 ULP before and 1.3 ULP after the fix, so a bf16-only sweep has little power to distinguish the two. ## Root cause ### 1. Inputs at and below `x = -4` return the raw input The current kernel initializes `result = x`, negates its local copy of `x`, and then has only two predicates ([`ckernel_sfpu_logsigmoid.h#L32-L54`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/tt_metal/hw/ckernels/wormhole_b0/metal/llk_api/llk_sfpu/ckernel_sfpu_logsigmoid.h#L32-L54)): ```cpp sfpi::vFloat result = x; x = -x; v_if(x < -4.0f) { result = -exp_neg_x; } v_elseif(x >= -4.0f && x < 4.0f) { result = -poly(x); } v_endif; ``` For the original input `x <= -4`, neither predicate is true. The output stays equal to the input and drops the `log1p(exp(x))` residual. At `x = -4`, the absolute error is 1.81e-2 and the relative error is 0.452%. ### 2. The positive tail uses a one-term series and approximate `exp` For `x > 4`, the kernel returns `-exp(-x)`. This replaces `log1p(e)` with `e` and drops the `-e^2/2` term, producing 0.91% relative error just above `x = 4`. The compute kernel also calls `exp_tile(1)` ([`logsigmoid_kernel.cpp#L40`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/eltwise/unary/device/kernels/compute/logsigmoid_kernel.cpp#L40)), so approximate-exp error is added to the truncation error. ### 3. The mid-range polynomial is inaccurate The degree-8 polynomial misses `ln(2)` by 7.12e-4 at `x = 0`, the centre of its fit range. On the common residual domain `[0, 4]`, the degree-8 polynomial in the adjacent `softplus` kernel has 48 times lower maximum absolute error. Representative values from the source-level model: | x | current | exact | relative error | regime | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---| | -4.0 | -4.000000000 | -4.018149928 | 0.452% | missing branch | | -1.0 | -1.306191057 | -1.313261688 | 0.538% | polynomial | | 0.0 | -0.692435443 | -0.693147181 | 0.103% | polynomial | | 1.0 | -0.315017842 | -0.313261688 | 0.561% | polynomial | | 4.0001 | -0.018313805 | -0.018148127 | 0.913% | one-term tail | The Wormhole and Blackhole headers differ in types and loop annotations, but their arithmetic is identical. ## Why tests miss it The main sweep draws from `torch_random(low=-4, high=10)` ([`log_sigmoid.py#L58`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/tests/sweep_framework/sweeps/eltwise/unary/log_sigmoid/log_sigmoid.py#L58)). It cannot sample below the missing branch boundary, and it covers only `bfloat16` and `bfloat8_b`. The same lower bound appears in four additional test entries. The existing LLK comparison uses `atol=0.05, rtol=0.05`. For positive inputs the output is a small residual, so the absolute tolerance can accept an incorrect result outright. ## Proposed fix Use one stable identity with no `+/-4` range split: ``` logsigmoid(x) = min(x, 0) - log1p(exp(-|x|)) ``` The exponential input is never positive, so the intermediate cannot overflow. In the actual FTZ implementation its result is in `[0, 1]`. Both required primitives already exist: the accurate path in `ckernel_sfpu_exp.h` and `calculate_log1p_fp32` in [`ckernel_sfpu_log1p.h#L52`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/main/tt_metal/hw/ckernels/wormhole_b0/metal/llk_api/llk_sfpu/ckernel_sfpu_log1p.h#L52). The proposed patch: - computes `exp(-|x|)` instead of `exp(-x)`; - switches `exp` to accurate mode; - replaces the range split with `calculate_log1p_fp32` plus the `x < 0` linear term; - applies the change to Wormhole and Blackhole; - widens all five `low=-4` test sites to `[-30, 30]` and adds fp32 coverage; - adds end-to-end fp32 and bf16 ULP tests. ## Validation Completed locally: - LLK path compiles with `-Werror` on Wormhole and Blackhole; - the actual `logsigmoid_kernel.cpp` compute translation unit passes a fake-JIT device-code compile check on Wormhole and Blackhole; - patched Wormhole kernel passes all four bf16-input `ttsim` configurations; - with identical stimuli and an error-sensitive tolerance, the current kernel fails the two fp32-DEST configurations and the patched kernel passes them; - source models replay `_sfpu_exp_fp32_accurate_` and `calculate_log1p_fp32` in float32, including both fused and non-fused MAD evaluation; - the two C++ callers of `calculate_logsigmoid` are updated. Limitations: - `ttsim` v1.10.1 aborts on Float32 input with fp32 DEST. The same failure occurs in its Float32 datacopy control, so this is not specific to `log_sigmoid`. The fp32 result needs device CI. - The full tt-metal runtime JIT generation and link were not run locally. The compute translation unit itself was compiled as described above. - No performance claim is made. Static Wormhole counts increase from 143 to 168 SFPU instructions for fp32 DEST and decrease from 143 to 70 for bf16 DEST; device timing is required. - In `ttsim`, both the current and patched paths return zero once the exponential becomes subnormal. This establishes no simulated regression; silicon behaviour still needs CI. The `ttsim` test plan below contains the commands, expected results and the full set of limitations. ## `ttsim` test plan
Reproducible ttsim test plan: setup, commands, results, expected results after the fix, and limitations Run on 2026-08-19 and 2026-08-20 on an Apple Silicon Mac in a Debian arm64 container. Everything marked *result* below was executed. What ttsim cannot run is marked as such, with the reason. --- #### Setup Host: Apple Silicon (arm64) macOS, Docker/colima. The toolchain and `ttsim` were both aarch64; no x86_64 emulation was used. ```bash # 1. Toolchain (hash-pinned by tt-metal itself, tt_metal/tt-llk/tests/sfpi-version) cd $TT_METAL_HOME/tt_metal/tt-llk/tests && ./setup_testing_env.sh # 2. Simulator + SoC descriptor mkdir -p ~/sim && cd ~/sim wget https://github.com/tenstorrent/ttsim/releases/download/v1.10.1/libttsim_wh_aarch64.so cp $TT_METAL_HOME/tt_metal/soc_descriptors/wormhole_b0_80_arch.yaml soc_descriptor.yaml # 3. Python env. Drop tt-smi from requirements.txt: its pyluwen dependency needs a Rust # toolchain and nothing in the simulator flow uses it. python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r $TT_METAL_HOME/tt_metal/tt-llk/tests/requirements.txt # 4. Run the four bf16-input configurations export TT_METAL_SIMULATOR=~/sim/libttsim_wh_aarch64.so export TT_METAL_DISABLE_SFPLOADMACRO=1 export CHIP_ARCH=wormhole cd $TT_METAL_HOME/tt_metal/tt-llk/tests/python_tests ID=test_sfpu_binary.py::test_sfpu_binary_logsigmoid DESELECT="" for out in Float16_b Float32; do for dest in No Yes; do DESELECT="$DESELECT --deselect $ID[formats:Float32->$out-mathop:SfpuLogsigmoid-dest_acc:$dest]" done; done pytest --run-simulator -q test_sfpu_binary.py -k logsigmoid $DESELECT # -> 4 passed, 1874 deselected ``` The four fp32-input configurations have to be deselected by node id, not with `-k "not Float32"`: that expression also drops the two `Float16_b->Float32` cases, which are bf16-input and do run. Two of the fp32-input ones abort the simulator (see Limitations) and an abort ends the session. System packages the toolchain needs beyond a bare `debian:bookworm`: `libmpc3` (`cc1plus`) and `libatomic1` (`tt_umd`). #### Checks and results | # | check | result | |---|---|---| | 1 | Kernel compiles, Wormhole + Blackhole, `-Werror` | **pass**, no warnings | | 1a | Actual `logsigmoid_kernel.cpp` translation unit, fake-JIT device compile, Wormhole + Blackhole | **pass**; only the pinned SFPI headers' existing warnings | | 2 | Canonical smoke test (`test_eltwise_unary_datacopy`, Float16_b, 4 faces) | **pass** | | 3 | `test_sfpu_binary_logsigmoid`, 4 bf16-input configs, patched kernel | **4 passed** | | 4 | Same 4 configs, **upstream** kernel `d7f34157`, shared tolerance | **4 passed** — the tolerance cannot see the defect | | 5 | Same 4 configs, uniform `atol=0, rtol=1e-2` (one to two bf16 ULP: one ULP of that format is 0.39–0.78% relative depending on position in the binade) | patched **4 pass**; upstream **2 fail, 2 pass** — the two failures are the fp32-DEST configs | | 6 | Threshold sweep, patched kernel, bf16 in / fp32 DEST | passes down to `rtol=5e-4` | | 7 | Threshold sweep, upstream kernel, same config | fails at `5e-3` and `1e-2`, passes only at `2e-2` | | 8 | Same sweep with **bf16 DEST** (`dest_acc:No`) | patched needs `>= 1e-2` — **not separable** from upstream, and left on the shared tolerance rather than papered over | | 9 | The tolerances proposed for the fix PR, both kernels | patched **4/4 pass**; upstream **2 fail** (the two fp32-DEST configs), 2 pass (the bf16-DEST ones, per row 8) | Row 9 is the one that matters for review: the PR does not merely add a test that passes, it adds one that fails on the kernel being replaced, on two of the four simulated configurations. Rows 6-8 are why the thresholds are where they are: 5e-4 vs 1e-2 leaves an order of magnitude of margin on each side, and where no such margin exists the test says so instead of inventing one. Rows 4 and 5 are the before/after. Row 4 shows why the defect survived: the LLK harness compares at `atol=0.05, rtol=0.05`, five times looser than the error being looked for. Row 5 holds the stimuli, the simulator and the criterion fixed and varies only the kernel. Neither row separates the two kernels in bf16 DEST. Nothing does, per row 8. #### Expected results after the fix - every `logsigmoid` config on bf16 input: pass; - the two fp32-DEST configs fail on the pre-fix kernel and pass on the patched one (`atol=0, rtol=5e-3`), which is the regression guard to re-run first; - `Float32 -> Float32, dest_acc=Yes` (silicon CI only, see Limitations): passes at `atol=0, rtol=1e-5`. The upstream kernel is 9.1e-3 relative there and fails it, and so would the `-softplus(-x)` reformulation this fix was chosen over (6.4e-5). This is the check that guards fp32 accuracy, and it is in the PR; - bf16 DEST: both kernels pass. Documented in the test, not hidden. #### Limitations 1. **No fp32 configuration of this op can run.** ttsim aborts on Float32 input tiles when DEST accumulation is on: `UndefinedBehavior: tensix_unpacr: unpack_to_dst=0 in_data_format=0 out_data_format=0`. This is not specific to this op — `test_eltwise_unary_datacopy[formats:Float32->Float32-dest_acc:Yes]` fails identically, while the same test's `dest_acc:No` configurations pass. Since fp32 input requires fp32 DEST, and the harness skips fp32-input/`dest_acc:No` (`_skip_fp32_no_dest_acc`), neither fp32 configuration is available. The headline number here is an fp32 number, so **ttsim cannot demonstrate it**; that needs device CI. 2. **bf16 caps the resolution anyway.** The harness computes its golden at the *input* format, and the second operand (`exp(-|x|)`) is quantized to the tile format, so a bf16 run cannot resolve better than ~0.4% relative whatever the kernel does. 3. **The bf16 gain is modest.** Modelled max error goes from 2.1 to 1.3 bf16 ULP (`|err| / ULP(exact)`, ULP = 2^(E-7) for bfloat16) — roughly one ULP of the format. The fp32 path is where it is five orders of magnitude off (9.1e-3 -> 2.15e-7 relative against the registered PyTorch golden in the fused-MAD model). This is an fp32 defect, which a bf16-only sweep could never have caught. 4. **`SFPLOADMACRO` must be disabled** (`TT_METAL_DISABLE_SFPLOADMACRO=1`), per TTSIM.md. With it disabled the SFPU path runs clean, no unimplemented-opcode error. 5. **No performance claim.** ttsim is functional only; cycle counts need silicon. 6. **The full runtime JIT was not run.** The actual compute translation unit compiles for both architectures, but local validation did not generate, link and execute it through a built tt-metal runtime. 7. The aarch64 `.so` is not hash-pinned in `tests/ttsim-version` (only the x86_64 ones are). Ours came from the official v1.10.1 release, the version the repo pins. #### Note on the golden `BinarySFPUGolden._logsigmoid` ignored its second operand and recomputed the exponential from `x`. That made the comparison measure the operand tile's quantization rather than the kernel. It now consumes the operand actually handed to the kernel. The operand generator also computes `exp(-|x|)` from `x` after input-format quantization, matching the device pipeline. End-to-end accuracy of the ttnn op stays covered by the ttnn tests (`test_unary_fp32.py`, `test_activation.py`).
## Prior art - #26958 investigated accurate `logsigmoid` implementations. Its best reported trade-offs were about 2 ULP at +43% kernel time and 4 ULP at +11%. - #32461 (merged) added the current SFPU kernel and evaluated bf16, not fp32. - #41390 (closed, unmerged) proposed `-softplus(-x)` and evaluated bf16 only. That is adequate for bf16 but models at about 1,000 fp32 ULP because the softplus residual fit targets absolute, not relative, accuracy. ## Acceptance criteria - fp32 output within 4 ULP of the registered PyTorch golden on `[-30, 30]`; - no discontinuity at `x = +/-4`; - fp32, bf16 and both tails covered by regression tests; - Wormhole and Blackhole CI pass; - behaviour outside the validated fp32 range is documented.
